title: Member Services Training Notes: Security Deposit Interest Credits and a Payment Arrangements Payoff
content:
**Member services training — Security Deposits interest credits at a Payment Arrangements (Deferred Payment Agreements) early payoff**

**The rule.** Deposit interest credits among the bill credits considered at an early payoff are applied to the payoff according to the Security Deposits record on the service account:

- at 100 percent (1.0) of their amount where the security deposit on the service account is held and was paid in full at least 24 calendar months before the payoff day;
- at 50 percent (0.5) of their amount where it is held and was paid in full more recently;
- not at all where no deposit is held on the service account.

**Questions answered in training**

*Which deposit is read?* The security deposit recorded on the same service account as the agreement, with its status and the date it was paid in full.

*How are the 24 months measured?* In calendar months, from the date the deposit was paid in full to the payoff day. A deposit paid in full exactly 24 months before the payoff day meets the 24-month line; one paid in full 23 months before is applied at 50 percent.

*What if the deposit was refunded or applied before the payoff?* A deposit no longer held on the service account gives no share: its interest credits are not applied.

| Deposit on the service account | Paid in full before the payoff day | Share of the deposit interest credits applied |
|---|---|---|
| held | 24 months or more | 100 percent |
| held | fewer than 24 months | 50 percent |
| not held | — | none |

**Hypothetical:** a deposit interest credit of $18.40 among the credits considered is applied as $18.40 where the deposit was paid in full 30 months earlier and as $9.20 where it was paid in full 10 months earlier.
